title: Deploy: systemd service files
description:
Create contrib/systemd/ directory and write two unit files: kithd.service (single-user) and kithd@.service (multi-user template). No Rust code changes.

What: Provide production-ready systemd unit files for deploying kithd.

Algorithm:
1. Create contrib/systemd/ directory
2. Write contrib/systemd/kithd.service:
   - [Unit] Description, After=network-online.target tailscaled.service, Requires=tailscaled.service
   - [Service] Type=simple (not notify; kithd has no sd_notify)
   - User=kithd, Group=kithd, UMask=0077
   - Environment lines: KITHD_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/kithd, KITHD_PORT=443, KITHD_OWNER_ID=<your-tailscale-user-id>, KITHD_TAILSCALED_SOCKET=/var/run/tailscale/tailscaled.sock, RUST_LOG=kithd=info,kith_peer=info
   - ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/kithd
   - Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=5
   - Security hardening: NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/kithd, ProtectHome=yes, PrivateTmp=yes, RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX AF_INET AF_INET6, CapabilityBoundingSet=, AmbientCapabilities=, LimitNOFILE=65536
   - StandardOutput=journal, StandardError=journal, SyslogIdentifier=kithd
   - [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target
   - Every directive MUST have a brief inline comment explaining why
3. Write contrib/systemd/kithd@.service (template, %i = username):
   - Description=Kith mailbox daemon for %i
   - User=kith-%i, Group=kithd, UMask=0077
   - Environment=KITHD_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/kithd/%i
   - SyslogIdentifier=kithd-%i
   - ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/kithd/%i
   - Otherwise same hardening as single-user file
   - Comment explaining %i substitution and per-user isolation

Defensive programming rules:
- Every directive must have an inline comment — no unexplained magic values
- KITHD_OWNER_ID line must have a comment saying 'get from: tailscale status --json | jq .Self.UserID'
- Do NOT add ReadWritePaths for /tmp (PrivateTmp=yes handles it)
- CapabilityBoundingSet= (empty) is correct — kithd binds to Tailscale interfaces which are non-privileged; port 443 on tailnet does not need CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE
- Do NOT add Type=notify — kithd does not call sd_notify; must stay Type=simple

Tests:
- Verify both files parse as valid systemd syntax using: systemd-analyze verify contrib/systemd/kithd.service (if systemd available)
- Review that security directives are present and correct
